research_scope: One mathematically reviewed candidate alias: the residue class x mod f in k[x]/(f) is a root of f over the quotient field, invoking the same polynomial root meaning as ordinary field extension zeros, without merging a multiple root or monic polynomial.

aliases.reason: For any field k and nonconstant irreducible f∈k[x], the canonical quotient k[x]/(f) is a field and α=x+(f) satisfies f(α)=0 by the quotient relation. Thus the phrase 'class of x as a root of f' instantiates the same contextual root concept as an arbitrary polynomial zero in an extension field. The quotient construction and choice of α remain extra source details. Repeated roots and monic polynomials are separate concepts.
